record.title: Apple describes a five-model foundation-model family with prompt-routed NAND-resident weights on device
record.summary: In a June 8, 2026 research announcement, Apple described its third-generation Foundation Models as a five-model family spanning on-device and Private Cloud Compute deployment. Apple says AFM 3 Core Advanced is a 20-billion-parameter sparse model that activates 1 to 4 billion parameters at a time; its full model weights reside in NAND, with a dense block selecting experts per prompt and periodically during generation. Apple attributes the design to instruction-following pruning research. The company also says AFM 3 Cloud Pro extends Private Cloud Compute to NVIDIA GPUs in Google Cloud with Google and NVIDIA. These are first-party architecture and deployment statements, not independent performance measurements or a public reproduction.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Apple published a June 8, 2026 overview describing a five-model third-generation Apple Foundation Model family spanning on-device and Private Cloud Compute deployment.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Apple says AFM 3 Core Advanced is a natively multimodal 20B-parameter sparse model that activates 1 to 4 billion parameters depending on the request, stores full weights in NAND and selects experts at prompt level.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Apple says AFM 3 Cloud Pro extends Private Cloud Compute to NVIDIA GPUs in Google Cloud through work with Google and NVIDIA, while maintaining Apple’s stated privacy guarantees. This review did not independently audit those guarantees.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent performance or systems evaluation of NAND-resident, prompt-routed AFM 3 Core Advanced was located.
The announcement does not identify the precise public operating-system release and device matrix for each model, or provide operational audit evidence for the stated Private Cloud Compute guarantees.

brief.importance_rationale: If the described architecture performs as stated, it could materially change the memory hierarchy available to on-device sparse inference by keeping a 20B-parameter model in flash while activating a small prompt-selected subset. The announcement does not establish measured throughput, energy, quality, cost or independent operation.
limitations: Architecture, performance and privacy statements are first-party Apple claims; no independent evaluation was performed.
No measured latency, throughput, energy, memory traffic, quality, cost or matched baseline is reported in the overview reviewed here.
The June 8 announcement is older than the 36-hour freshness window and does not establish a new event in this activation.
The exact public software release, eligible-device matrix, current deployment state and independent validation of Private Cloud Compute guarantees were not checked.
brief.summary: In a June 8, 2026 research announcement, Apple described its third-generation Foundation Models as a five-model family spanning on-device and Private Cloud Compute deployment. Apple says AFM 3 Core Advanced is a 20-billion-parameter sparse model that activates 1 to 4 billion parameters at a time; its full model weights reside in NAND, with a dense block selecting experts per prompt and periodically during generation. Apple attributes the design to instruction-following pruning research. The company also says AFM 3 Cloud Pro extends Private Cloud Compute to NVIDIA GPUs in Google Cloud with Google and NVIDIA. These are first-party architecture and deployment statements, not independent performance measurements or a public reproduction.

technical.claimed_result: Apple describes AFM 3 Core Advanced as a natively multimodal 20B-parameter sparse model that activates 1–4B parameters depending on the request, and says the five-model third-generation family spans device and Private Cloud Compute deployments.
technical.compute_or_cost: Apple gives a 20B total parameter count and 1–4B active range for AFM 3 Core Advanced, but no latency, throughput, energy, cost or flash-to-memory bandwidth measurements were verified in this review.
technical.demonstrated_result: Apple published a dated first-party technical overview describing the five model variants, the stated AFM 3 Core Advanced parameter counts and routing design, and a Google/NVIDIA Cloud extension for AFM 3 Cloud Pro. This verifies what Apple publicly announced, not independent model operation or performance.
technical.implementation_status: Announced June 8, 2026. Apple describes models as integrated into its operating systems but this review did not inspect a specific public software release, deployment configuration or supported-device matrix.
technical.mechanism: Apple says AFM 3 Core Advanced stores its full sparse model in NAND rather than requiring all weights in DRAM. A lightweight dense block selects a fixed expert set during prompt processing and periodically reselects experts during generation; shared experts remain active while routed experts move to DRAM as needed. Apple attributes the model to instruction-following pruning (IFP).
technical.novelty: The announced design combines prompt-level expert selection with a full sparse model stored in flash, instead of loading token-specific experts from NAND on every generation step. The announcement attributes this approach to Apple IFP research; performance novelty is not independently established.
technical.regime: A provider-described Apple Intelligence model family integrated with Apple operating systems: two on-device variants and three server models on Private Cloud Compute. AFM 3 Cloud Pro is described as running on NVIDIA GPUs in Google Cloud. Independent availability and hardware coverage were not verified.
technical.reproducibility: The architecture overview is public, but model weights, detailed evaluation protocol, deployment code and independent test data were not inspected or located in this pass.
technical.strongest_baseline: Apple contrasts its design with conventional dense or sparsely activated models that require all weights in active DRAM and describes standard token-by-token MoE swapping as limited by NAND-to-DRAM bandwidth. The announcement does not provide matched baseline measurements.

brief.title: Apple describes a five-model foundation-model family with prompt-routed NAND-resident weights on device
brief.why_it_matters: If the described design operates as stated, prompt-level expert loading from flash could change the memory tradeoffs for running larger sparse models on consumer devices. The announcement also signals a private-cloud deployment path spanning Apple, Google Cloud and NVIDIA. No independent evidence establishes its latency, energy, quality, privacy properties in operation or supported-device coverage.
